The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law, followed by federal treaties and statutes (generally coequal, with the later-in-time one controlling when they conflict), then federal regulations, then state constitutions, state statutes, state regulations, and local ordinances. Under the Supremacy Clause, valid federal law overrides conflicting state law. The shared team note is wrong to put treaties and statutes above the Constitution, since both must comply with it, and its placement of executive agreements is also not a settled ranking.

CONFIDENCE: 85
